Open Questions — spark-facilitator
Opportunity-level, durable across runs. Every run must read ## Open before raising questions of its own, and must record — in that run's PDD § Open Questions — whether it resolves, carries forward, or contradicts each row.


## Archive is closed history: never read back, never inlined at phase handoff. Resolution MOVES a row from ## Open to ## Archive; it never annotates one in place.


Each row carries a single latest: holding the CURRENT state only, replaced (not appended to) by each run. Do not re-introduce per-run annotation stacking.

Open
* id: cbf-smartphones-and-connectivity question: Do the CBFs who would be in the pilot have smartphones able to run the Connect app, and adequate connectivity? raised_by: 20260817-1610 owner: Spark / awarded LLO answered_where: solicitation responses blocking: Go/no-go. If the answer is no, the pilot cannot run as designed. latest: Unanswered. Evidence points against assuming smartphones: Spark's own FIYP programme provisions offline-first Samsung A9 tablets (~$150) with headphones and power banks, distributed by file share rather than download — a stack chosen because connectivity could not be assumed. Connect requires a smartphone and a PersonalID. The solicitation requires the responding LLO to confirm availability explicitly.


* id: cbf-compensation-baseline question: What does Spark pay CBFs today — volunteer, stipend, or per-activity — and who pays it? raised_by: 20260817-1610 owner: Spark answered_where: solicitation responses blocking: Before Phase 8 latest: Run 20260925-1536 now writes a [PROPOSED] band (MWK 5,000–10,000 per verified meeting to the CBF, plus MWK 3,000 per meeting to the implementing organisation, a floor the LLO is asked to re-cost) because the design rules require Phase 4 to have a number. The band is an ACE placeholder with no sourced anchor; the solicitation asks for current CBF compensation, a local reference rate, and a justified rate against the PDD's hours table (~5.5–7.5 h of work per paid meeting, ~3 h of it paid).


* id: cross-phase-income-cliff question: About 60% of a CBF's lifetime payable meetings fall in the first 26% of the FCAP arc, so a flat per-meeting rate produces roughly a fourfold monthly income drop when Planning ends — for a role that continues another 16 months. Should the rate be phase-differentiated, or paired with a retainer? raised_by: 20260828-0703 owner: Spark answered_where: — blocking: Before Phase 8 latest: Re-derived independently by run 20260906-2233 from Enock Q&A §1 (weekly in planning, monthly otherwise) and the FCAP Structure durations: ~24 of ~40 lifetime meetings fall in the first 5.5 months of 21.5. The pilot ends inside Goal Setting and never reaches the cliff, so it is stated but not priced. Interacts directly with cbf-compensation-baseline.


* id: continuation-meeting-reduced-payment question: Should a continuation meeting on an already-paid FCAP step carry a reduced payment rather than nothing? raised_by: 20260817-1610 owner: Spark answered_where: — blocking: Before Phase 8 latest: Unchanged. Past the 3-per-step cap, real facilitation work earns zero. The cap was set generously for exactly this reason, but a reduced continuation rate remains the better answer if Spark wants one.


* id: per-step-payable-cap-value question: Is 3 payable meetings per community per FCAP step the right cap? raised_by: 20260820-0817 owner: Spark answered_where: — blocking: Before Phase 8. Sibling of continuation-meeting-reduced-payment. latest: Independently re-derived by run 20260906-2233: Planning is ~24 weekly meetings across 14 steps ≈ 1.7 meetings/step, so a cap of 3 is ~1.8x the modelled average and binds only where a step overruns. Still an ACE inference with no partner input.


* id: supervision-ratios question: What are the actual supervision ratios (Partner Trainer → CBFs, Field Officer → communities)? raised_by: 20260817-1610 owner: Spark answered_where: solicitation responses blocking: Before Phase 8 latest: Still unquantified by any source, and more load-bearing as of run 20260925-1536: Layer B is now risk-stratified (every flagged meeting reviewed, ≥20% overall) and Layer C adds community confirmation calls (≥10% of paid meetings), so Partner Trainer and supervisor capacity both matter. The solicitation asks the responding organisation to state it.


* id: pilot-district-and-communities question: Which Malawi district(s) and Traditional Authority for the pilot, and which communities enter FCAP Goal Setting in the pilot window? raised_by: 20260817-1610 owner: Spark / awarded LLO answered_where: solicitation responses; solicitation review blocking: Before Phase 4 latest: The pilot window is the Goal Setting subphase (FCAP steps 1–7, ~3 months) and the cohort is ~12 communities / 12 CBFs — an ACE projection, not partner-stated. The solicitation requires the district, Traditional Authority and candidate communities in the response.


* id: household-count-denominator question: Spark's attendance and savings indicators are percentages of "total # households in community". The pilot captures that count at community enrolment. Does Spark want a reconciliation against their own household data, and against which snapshot — and is any Spark indicator currently computed against hh_count_tt before household registration completes? raised_by: 20260820-0817 owner: Spark / ACE answered_where: — blocking: Before Phase 3 latest: ⚠ CONTRADICTION re-verified by run 20260907-1120 — the prior run's finding STANDS, with ONE CORRECTION to its quoted evidence. Correction: the prior row quoted a single bind, <bind nodeset="/data/case/update/hh_count_tt" calculate="0"/>. That exact bind does not exist in the CCZ. The seeding happens through TWO binds in modules-0/forms-0.xml — <bind nodeset="/data/hh_tt" calculate="0"/> feeding <bind nodeset="/data/case/update/hh_count_tt" calculate="/data/hh_tt" relevant="count(/data/hh_tt) &gt; 0"/>. Everything else is confirmed: (1) the Village Profile Form ASKS number_of_households (required, constraint=". <= 400") and average_household_size (required, 4–12) and DISCARDS both — neither appears in that form's <case><update> block; (2) the case value is seeded to zero at registration; (3) hh_count_tt is a RATCHETED COUNT OF REGISTERED HOUSEHOLDS raised one at a time by m0f1 (household_counter = hh_count_tt + 1), not the community's household count, and it reads 0 until RCT registration has run. Consequence unchanged: at Goal Setting time an attendance percentage against it is undefined or absurd, so the pilot capturing its own enrolment count is the ONLY figure that exists, not a workaround.


* id: fcap-step-numbering question: The FCAP Structure PDF's body carries 25 distinct step headings while its header states 24 steps, with the number 19 used twice ("Transition Timeline" closing Phase 2; "Needs, Pathways, Goal(s), and Vision" opening Phase 3). Are those two Step 19s one step or two — and is the intended total 24 or 25? raised_by: 20260828-0703 owner: Spark answered_where: — blocking: Before Phase 3 latest: ⚠ CONTRADICTION re-verified by run 20260907-1120 — the prior run's finding STANDS. The body carries 25 distinct Step N: headings: 1–24 each once, plus a second 19 — Step 19: Transition Timeline closing Phase 2 and Step 19: Needs, Pathways, Goal(s), and Vision opening Phase 3 — against a header stating 24 steps. Method note for future runs: a line-anchored grep -cE '^Step [0-9]+:' returns 24 and appears to REFUTE this, because the second Step 19 is preceded by a form-feed page break (\f); a whitespace-tolerant match returns 25. The two headings' objectives differ, which argues they are distinct steps, but the document does not say. The pilot declares only its own window (steps 1–7, unambiguous because the duplication starts at 19) and records the 25-heading taxonomy as OBSERVED. No pilot payment is affected either way.


* id: savings-block-relevance-deviation question: Spark's currently_saving is required="true()" with no relevance condition, so it is asked at every meeting — including Goal Setting steps 1–4, before community-wide savings are introduced at Step 5. The pilot gates the savings block on the step pointer, deviating from the source instrument. Does Spark want the pilot to match the source form's behaviour instead — and is Spark's own "% of Communities saving" indicator biased downward by pre-Step-5 meetings that structurally cannot report savings? raised_by: 20260828-0703 owner: Spark M&E answered_where: — blocking: Before Phase 3 latest: Re-verified against modules-0/forms-4.xml by run 20260906-2233: the bind carries required="true()" and no relevant attribute. The pilot gates on pilot_fcap_step >= step_5 and discloses the deviation rather than making it silently.


* id: lookup-table-provisioning question: The v1392 app depends on 12 lookup tables (malawi_steps, malawi_green_fcap_villages, malawi_green_cbfs, malawi_green_pts, malawi_green_disctrict, malawi_green_ta, malawi_group_of_village, malawi_green_village_uuids, malawi_green_patner, foccad_activities, malawi_activities, project_type_fvs). The pilot needs at minimum a step list and the community identity tables. Will Spark supply these as data, or should the pilot maintain its own? raised_by: 20260828-0703 owner: Spark / ACE answered_where: — blocking: Before Phase 3 latest: Re-verified by run 20260906-2233: the CCZ carries these tables only as itemset REFERENCES, never as data — no fixture files ship in the zip. The pilot mints its own step_1…step_7 codes with labels read verbatim from the FCAP Structure PDF, and carries an explicit reconciliation residual so a later mapping onto Spark's real step_id codes is a lookup rather than a re-read.


* id: gps-capture-acceptability question: Spark's app already captures GPS at village registration but deliberately not per meeting. Is a location fix on each community meeting acceptable to Spark and to the communities, and does capturing it at a public village meeting raise any consent concern? raised_by: 20260820-0817 owner: Spark answered_where: — blocking: Before Phase 3 latest: The correction first recorded by run 20260828-0703 was RE-VERIFIED against the CCZ by run 20260906-2233: five type="geopoint" binds exist — m0f0 gps_coordinates_of_the_community, m0f1 Q14, m0f2 gps_coordinates, m0f10 ESSCL-OLD, m0f11 project_info/gps — and the per-meeting Village Monitoring Form (m0f4) has zero. So enrolment GPS mirrors m0f0 exactly and is NOT net-new; only the per-meeting capture is a genuinely new ask. Acceptability and consent remain unanswered.


* id: phase-pointer-maintenance question: Spark's Village Profile Update Form maintains community phase movement and is out of the pilot slice. Should the pilot advance the FCAP step pointer from its own monitoring form, or pull the Village Profile Update Form into scope? raised_by: 20260820-0817 owner: Spark / ACE answered_where: — blocking: Before Phase 3 latest: ⚠ CONTRADICTION upheld by run 20260925-1536. Four forms write Spark's phase (modules-0/forms-0.xml, forms-3.xml, forms-5.xml, forms-8.xml); the Village Monitoring Form (forms-4.xml) does not, so the pilot keeps its own pilot_fcap_step and never writes phase. New evidence: forms-4.xml asks the CBF "Which FCAP step is the Village in?" at every meeting (a select over malawi_steps filtered by phase); the pilot instead READS the step from the community record and advances it only via a step-completed answer, so the same content cannot be paid under several steps. Spark should say whether it prefers its own behaviour or wants m0f3 in scope.


* id: pilot-record-instead-of-or-in-addition question: During the pilot, do CBFs file the pilot record instead of, or in addition to, Spark's Village Monitoring Form? raised_by: 20260817-1610 owner: Spark answered_where: — blocking: Before Phase 6 latest: Only Spark can answer — the Village Monitoring Form feeds a live RCT, so ACE cannot decide to displace it. Cost quantified by run 20260906-2233 and carried as an explicit unpaid-work row in the PDD: "in addition to" means double entry of the same meeting into two systems at ~4.3 meetings/CBF/month during Goal Setting, unpaid under a unit that pays once.


* id: connect-markers-in-sparks-own-app question: Would Spark prefer, as the end state, that Connect markers be added to Spark's own HQ app rather than running a parallel pilot app? raised_by: 20260817-1610 owner: Spark answered_where: — blocking: Before closeout latest: New evidence from run 20260906-2233: the v1392 app has ZERO Connect markers — grep -c 'commcareconnect' across all 60 form XMLs returns 0, as does a search for the legacy learn: prefix. So this is not "add a few markers to an app that mostly has them"; it would be first instrumentation of an app a live four-arm RCT depends on. The pilot's verbatim reuse of Spark's field paths and raw value codes keeps the option cheap either way.


* id: fiyp-media-assets question: Can Spark share the FIYP media assets (35 presenter-to-camera videos, 12 community videos, 280+ slides) for the Learn app? raised_by: 20260817-1610 owner: Spark answered_where: — blocking: Before Phase 3 latest: Not blocking — the Learn app is scoped to recording competence and payment-model facts rather than reproducing Spark's facilitation curriculum. Run 20260906-2233 names the specific ask: the FIYP library's "Running an Effective Meeting" interview/walkthrough with a real CBF maps directly onto Learn Module 2, which is the module whose quality most affects data reliability.


* id: app-runtime-default-language question: Should the app open in Chichewa or Tumbuka rather than English? raised_by: 20260817-1610 owner: Spark answered_where: — blocking: Before Phase 6 latest: Narrowed to the runtime default only. The app carries nya and tum strings on an always-complete English source; that half is settled. Run 20260906-2233 adds that Spark's OWN app opens in English (cur_locale is en in the CCZ profile), so English-first matches what a CBF already using the Spark app would expect. Note the translations are ACE-authored and marked needs-review, not native-speaker reviewed.


* id: proposal-generator-boundary question: The FCAP Structure PDF says CBFs enter agreed actions and budgets into a Proposal Generator at steps 10, 11 and 12; the FIYP overview describes it as a separate offline Flutter app that outputs XLS shared via WhatsApp. It is not part of the CommCare app. If the pilot extends into Proposal Development, where is the boundary between Connect-verified work and Proposal Generator work? raised_by: 20260828-0703 owner: Spark / ACE answered_where: — blocking: Before any extension into Proposal Development. Non-blocking for the Goal Setting pilot, whose window ends at step 7.


* id: rwanda-two-cbf-attribution question: For expansion beyond Malawi: how is payment attributed where two CBFs share one community (Rwanda)? raised_by: 20260817-1610 owner: Spark answered_where: — blocking: Before expansion latest: Two design elements assume 1:1 coverage and both break at 2:1 — case ownership (a meeting is payable only from the CBF who owns the community case) and the entity_id grain, which would collapse two co-facilitators' records onto one payable key. Malawi, Uganda and Ghana are 1:1 and unaffected.


* id: progression-affects-payment question: Should on-time phase progression eventually affect payment, or remain monitoring-only? raised_by: 20260817-1610 owner: ACE / Spark answered_where: — blocking: Post-pilot latest: Pilot position restated: monitoring-only. A community can stall for reasons a competent CBF does not control — season, a contested secret-ballot election (Step 2), a delayed microgrant tranche, or the Proposal Review Committee's turnaround (Step 13) — and pricing progression would move programme risk onto the lowest-paid actor. Spark's own on-time-progression indicator is reported as primary metric P3 without being priced.


* id: assessment-item-rotation question: Does retake-resistance on the Learn assessment matter enough to warrant a Nova capability request for per-attempt item rotation? raised_by: 20260817-1610 owner: ACE answered_where: — blocking: Non-blocking latest: Framing unchanged and still correct: per-attempt rotation is NOT a platform impossibility — it is expressible in XForms (a seeded draw from a fixture nodeset, or hidden questions gated on relevant), and Connect scores a fixed-size draw normally. What is missing is a Nova authoring primitive. This is a capability request to file, not a limitation to design around. Relevant because the pilot allows unlimited retakes against a fixed 12-item bank.


* id: savings-indicator-denominator-bias question: Spark's currently_saving is asked at every meeting with no relevance condition, including Goal Setting steps 1–4 where community-wide savings have not yet been introduced (they begin at FCAP Step 5). Does that bias Spark's own "% of Communities saving" indicator downward by including meetings that structurally cannot report savings? raised_by: 20260907-1120 owner: Spark M&E answered_where: — blocking: Non-blocking for the pilot latest: Raised by run 20260907-1120 as the mirror of savings-block-relevance-deviation. That row asks whether the PILOT should match Spark's form; this one asks whether Spark's OWN indicator is affected. The pilot's S5 metric restricts its denominator to communities at Step 5 or later for exactly this reason. ACE cannot answer it — it is a question about Spark's reporting, not about the pilot.


* id: phase-authoritative-writer question: Phase movement in the v1392 app is written by four forms (m0f0, m0f3, m0f5, m0f8), not one. If Spark ever wants Connect markers added to their own app, which form is authoritative for phase movement? raised_by: 20260907-1120 owner: Spark answered_where: — blocking: Before any instrumentation of Spark's own app latest: Raised by run 20260907-1120 out of the phase-pointer-maintenance contradiction. Non-blocking for the pilot, which runs a parallel app and never writes Spark's phase. It becomes load-bearing the moment connect-markers-in-sparks-own-app is answered yes.


* id: program-currency-usd-vs-mwk question: The durable Connect program for this opp (a115e4f2…, ai-demo-space) was created with country MWI and currency USD; the design is denominated in Malawian kwacha and currency is create-time-only. Reuse the USD program and convert every figure at award, or create a replacement MWK program? raised_by: 20260925-1536 owner: Operator / ACE answered_where: Phase 4 connect-program-setup step 3b (escalates on currency divergence) blocking: Before Phase 4 latest: Raised by run 20260925-1536 after connect_get_program returned currency: USD, country: MWI, delivery_type: 14 (ace). The PDD declares opportunity_currency: MWK per the locale rule.


* id: connect-delivery-type-fit question: None of the 19 Connect delivery types on ai-demo-space describes community-meeting facilitation; the program runs as ace. Should the Connect team add a fitting type (e.g. "Community Facilitation")? raised_by: 20260925-1536 owner: Connect team answered_where: — blocking: Non-blocking latest: Raised by run 20260925-1536; the PDD declares connect_delivery_type: ace to match the existing, immutable program.


* id: layer-c-community-contact-calls question: Is Spark comfortable with the implementing organisation phoning each community's primary contact (a name and number Spark's own Village Profile Form already requires) to confirm a sample of meetings, with that contact's consent? raised_by: 20260925-1536 owner: Spark answered_where: — blocking: Before Phase 3 latest: Raised by run 20260925-1536, which adds Layer C as a ≥10% call sample in consenting communities to close the fabrication blind spot Layer A cannot see. Only the consent question is net-new; the contact fields are reused from modules-0/forms-0.xml.

* id: meeting-verification-predicate question: What is the concrete verification predicate for "a meeting happened"? raised_by: pre-ledger (ACE research brief, 2026-07-13) owner: Spark resolved_at: 2026-07-24T00:00:00Z resolved_by: Enock Tusingwire, Q&A §1; verified against the CCZ resolution_note: meeting_conducted = Yes AND meeting_type = Community meeting. Raw XForm values are yes and community_meeting; "Yes" / "Community meeting" are the English display labels. Re-verified against modules-0/forms-4.xml <value> elements by runs 20260820-0817, 20260828-0703 and 20260906-2233; meeting_type's only other value is committee_meeting.


* id: who-is-the-paid-facilitator question: Who is the paid facilitator? raised_by: pre-ledger (ACE research brief, 2026-07-13) owner: Spark resolved_at: 2026-07-24T00:00:00Z resolved_by: Enock Tusingwire, Q&A §2 resolution_note: The CBF — not the Partner Trainer, Finance Officer or GRM Focal Person.


* id: cbf-to-community-coverage question: How many communities does one CBF cover? raised_by: pre-ledger (ACE research brief, 2026-07-13) owner: Spark resolved_at: 2026-07-24T00:00:00Z resolved_by: Enock Tusingwire, Q&A §1 resolution_note: 1 CBF per community in Uganda, Malawi and Ghana; 2 per community in Rwanda. The Rwanda case remains live as rwanda-two-cbf-attribution in ## Open.


* id: meeting-cadence question: How often do FCAP community meetings run? raised_by: pre-ledger (ACE research brief, 2026-07-13) owner: Spark resolved_at: 2026-07-24T00:00:00Z resolved_by: Enock Tusingwire, Q&A §1 resolution_note: Weekly during the planning phase; monthly in the other phases.


* id: pilot-scope-focused-slice question: Is a focused first slice the right pilot scope? raised_by: pre-ledger (ACE research brief, 2026-07-13) owner: Spark resolved_at: 2026-07-24T00:00:00Z resolved_by: Enock Tusingwire, Q&A §3 resolution_note: Yes — facilitator registration + per-meeting monitoring + savings, rather than all ~41 forms.
